why: The west pit, taken out of its well and set on `anchor/case` — one cell, on the stone floor of the near hall, beside the chest a `collect` objective sends the party to. That cell is a `minecraft:chest`, so the volume's own cells are cells no body could ever walk into; what it catches is the RING around it, the eight cells at standing height whose occupant's hitbox reaches the box. A volume kills through a box selector and the server adjudicates a box selector on hitbox INTERSECTION, so those eight are cells a body dies in — and every one of them is plain stone floor that reads exactly like the rest of the hall. Danger is visible, or the engine refuses it: the refusal names the volume, the keep-out, and the floor cells by course, and it prescribes moving the HAZARD — lower it under the floor, draw its extent in, or lay a block vanilla hurts with under those cells and declare it in `shown_by`. It does not prescribe closing the walk graph, and that is the whole ruling: the compiler knows which stone kills and the player does not. It declares no unit — a lethal volume, its region and a `collect` objective on a container are each written by the gallery proper. What must not compile is a killing volume whose reach covers ground a player would read as safe. The route closure this also causes (`DW0510`) is its symptom, and is asked second on purpose: an author sent to `give the party a route around it` would be repairing the wrong thing.
